# Where the code comes from

Each game's decompilation is a git submodule: the project's own repository
at one commit, with OpenRAC's few changes kept beside it as patches. [CREDITS.md](../CREDITS.md) lists the people behind
each project.

Full hashes are in each `games/<game>/game.json`, under `decomp` (a game's own
decompilation) or a version's `source`. rac1-decomp
follows the [Veradictus fork](https://github.com/Veradictus/rac1-decomp)'s
`main`, so its commit may not be upstream yet.

## How it works

Each project is a git submodule. A game's decompilation holds every version of the game, so its
folder is the game's, not a version's: `games/<game>/decomp` (rac1-decomp, rac2-decomp, rac4-decomp
and the others), recorded in game.json's top-level `decomp` (`dir`, `repo`, `branch`, `commit`, ...),
and every version built from it has `"dir": "games/<game>/decomp"` and `"source": {"shared":
"decomp", ...}`. A project that holds one version only keeps that version's folder
(`games/rac1/ntsc`, the NTSC decomp, with its own `source`). Nothing is committed inside a project.
OpenRAC's changes are beside it, in `games/<game>/decomp-patches/` (or
`games/<game>/<version>-patches/`):

- `0001-Some-change.patch`: one change per file, with the reason in its message.
- `files/`: OpenRAC's own files, copied in as they are.
- `README.md`: the list of patches.

After a clone or a pull:

```sh
python3 tools/sources.py init    # git submodule update --init --depth 1, then apply
```

`unapply` removes the changes again, `status` shows each project.

## Moving a pin

A project's pin (its submodule commit and game.json's `"commit"`) and the port's tables made from it
move together: hostgen's config and tables, the release names and tables, the asm interfaces and the
Windows exports under `port/game/<game>*`. CI runs `tools/sources.py check --since <base>`, which
fails a pull request whose pin and game.json disagree, or which moves a pin without changing anything
under `port/game/<game>*`.

## Where a change goes

- **A change to the decomp** (a match, a name, a build fix): a pull request
  in the decomp's own repository. OpenRAC gets it with the next `update`.
- **A change only OpenRAC needs**: a patch, with its reason.

## Changing a patch

```sh
python3 tools/sources.py edit rac1/decomp  # the patches become commits in games/rac1/decomp
# in games/rac1/decomp: commit, amend or rebase as usual; one commit = one patch
python3 tools/sources.py save rac1/decomp  # the commits become patches again
```

Then commit the `-patches/` folder.

## Updating a project

```sh
python3 tools/sources.py update rac1/ntsc            # to the tip of its branch
python3 tools/sources.py update rac1/ntsc <commit>   # or to one commit
```

This moves the submodule, rebases the patches and writes the new commit to
`game.json`. On a conflict, fix it in the submodule, run
`git rebase --continue`, then `save`. Check the new commit against the
[sourcing policy](policy/SOURCING.md) and commit it as `chore(import)`.
After updating rac2/ntsc, also redo the port's name list
([port/game/rac2-ntsc](../port/game/rac2-ntsc/README.md#building-and-running)).

## Other projects OpenRAC builds on

These are credited where their work is used, and in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md):

- [ReRAC](https://github.com/re-rac/rerac) (ISC): the moby, collision and
  animation formats in the editor, and function notes in rac1/pal.
- [Wrench](https://github.com/chaoticgd/wrench) (GPL-3.0-or-later): asset
  formats, read for the editor; the tool rac2 and rac3 use to unpack discs.
- splat, spimdisasm, objdiff, asm-differ, decomp-permuter, m2c and wibo:
  the decompilation tooling the projects use; none is vendored here.
